name: PASTON
description: Paston is a three-player Armenian Preference-style trick-taking game from Gyumri. The declarer chooses trumps after bidding and must take at least six of ten tricks or surrender.

content.text: Paston is a three-player Armenian Preference-style trick-taking game from Gyumri. The declarer chooses trumps after bidding and must take at least six of ten tricks or surrender.
Rooted in the interaction between Eastern European trick-taking traditions and Middle Eastern social gaming. It bears strong similarities to 'Pastushok' and 'Preferans'.
Three players; no partnerships. The game is played mainly in Armenia (e.g. Gyumri). Deal, bidding and play are clockwise; each player plays for themselves toward 121 points.
Each player receives 10 cards (often dealt 2 at a time). 2 cards are placed face-down in the 'Prikup'.

items.text: Score when declarer surrenders: In some rules opponents do not score 2 points when the declarer surrenders; in others they do. Affects whether sacrifice bids are more attractive.
Paston grkha (best spades): Highest bid; spades are trump but with higher penalty for losing. Declarer scores only +10 for six tricks (not multiplied by 4); other scores multiplied by 4.
Redeal conditions: If bottom card is 7 of spades, cards are reshuffled and redealt. If a player holds 7-8-9-10-J-Q of spades but neither K nor A of spades, cards are shown and redealt by same dealer.
